title: Metheringham Airfield — 106 Squadron Memorial
memorial_address: Former airfield site, Metheringham, North Kesteven, Lincolnshire LN4 3TF
inscription: DEDICATED TO THE AIRMEN AND AIRWOMEN WHO SERVED ON AND WITH 106 SQUADRON IN WORLD WAR TWO 1939-1945 / 995 GAVE THEIR LIVES / LEST WE FORGET
crew_summary: 995 aircrew killed serving with 106 Squadron across World War Two
narrative: 106 Squadron flew Manchesters and Lancasters from RAF Metheringham in Lincolnshire, and before that from Coningsby and other stations. The squadron's war record was exceptional in scale and cost: 995 personnel killed across the conflict, with 59 Lancasters lost from Metheringham alone. Among the squadron's famous connections: Wing Commander Guy Gibson commanded 106 Squadron before forming 617 Squadron (Dambusters), and Sergeant Norman Cyril Jackson won the Victoria Cross during a Schweinfurt raid in April 1944, climbing out onto the wing of a burning Lancaster to extinguish an engine fire — an act of extraordinary courage. The memorial at the former airfield site near the Metheringham Airfield Visitor Centre is a brick structure in fireplace style, with a central incised tablet bearing 'PRO LIBERTATE' (For Freedom). Two flanking brass plaques carry an airfield map and full dedication text. A squadron badge recess and mountings for a Lancaster model complete the structure. The memorial was dedicated on 8 July 1992 and is complemented by a 990-name Roll of Honour in calligraphy held at the nearby visitor centre.
memorial_details: Central incised tablet with 'PRO LIBERTATE'. Two flanking brass plaques with airfield map and dedication. Squadron badge recess. Mountings for Lancaster model. Wooden bench with brass plaques. A 990-name Roll of Honour in calligraphy is held separately at Metheringham Airfield Visitor Centre (Westmoor Farm, Martin Moor, LN4 3WF). IWM War Memorials Register reference: IWM 20504.
